description: Renovate policy for schubergphilis/mdd; see docs/agents/dependency-updates.md. Run by .github/workflows/renovate.yml.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Vulnerability fixes wait the same 7 days as every other update. Renovate's default drops the wait for them, but a release rushed out as a 'security fix' is exactly what a supply-chain attack looks like. They still skip the Monday schedule.

packageRules.description: A new Python minor (3.14 -> 3.15) is a deliberate move, not a routine bump: the ML wheels (torch, via docling) lag behind, and .mise.toml pins UV_PYTHON for that reason. Keep it out of the non-major group and only open the PR once a maintainer approves it on the Dependency Dashboard.

Never move TypeScript to a new major. `astro check` goes through @astrojs/language-server, which needs the programmatic TypeScript API that TypeScript 7 does not ship yet: https://github.com/withastro/roadmap/discussions/1321

Lock file maintenance has no release timestamp, and a minimumReleaseAge without a timestamp stays pending forever. The transitives it pulls in are aged by each tool's own cooldown instead: exclude-newer in pyproject.toml, minimumReleaseAge in site/bunfig.toml, minimum_release_age in .mise.toml.

Renovate's own image (in .github/workflows/renovate.yml and the renovate-validate task in .mise.toml) is on GHCR, which has no release timestamps, so the 7-day wait would not apply. Look it up on npm instead, which has them; same versions.

Commit and PR titles are build(deps): ..., as in the rest of the history. config:recommended's semantic prefix preset sets fix for production dependencies and chore for the rest in packageRules, which override the top-level semanticCommitType, so this rule, last, sets it back.

customManagers.description: Renovate's image (`ghcr.io/renovatebot/renovate:<version>`) in the workflow that runs it and in the renovate-validate task. Both must be the same version.
